correctness.rationale: For a tree the incidence matrix B has rank N−1 and all maximal square minors ±1, giving det BᵀB=N by Cauchy–Binet and the cross-polytope image volume. Since the body is centrally symmetric, W_T=2 max_edges |U_i−U_j|. Spherical U=(G−Gbar 1)/R with independent standard Gaussians yields exactly W_T=2 max_edges|G_i−G_j|/R, and R/√N→1 at a faster rate than normal-extreme fluctuations. Edge-normalized differences of disjoint edges are independent and incident correlations have magnitude 1/2. For threshold b_(2m)+x/b_(2m), the Arratia–Goldstein–Gordon Poisson approximation first error is O(Δ/m), second O(Δ m^(−1/3)(log m)^(2/3)), both vanish by the stated Δ growth hypothesis; this gives Gumbel. Broom star edges maximize to b_n+|G_hub|+o_P(1), while path edges maximize to √2 b_(2ℓ)+O_P(1/b_(2ℓ)); the full maximum is exactly their max. The path remainder converges to zero without independence assumptions, yielding max(|Z|,s) and a point atom of mass 2Φ(s)−1 for s>0. For c_n→+∞ the path-centred finer Gumbel law transfers; explicit inverse-Gaussian-tail integer ℓ choice realizes all s. Independent exact Gram determinant checks for paths and stars on N=3..11 reproduced det(BᵀB)=N; numerical simulation is not the theorem proof.
residual_risks: Extreme-value proof assumes fixed real x while m→∞ and Δ=o(m^(1/3)/(log m)^(2/3)); no claim of necessity for this degree bound.
Independent Gram identity checked, but no complete independent simulation of source broom phase cases or formal proof of AGG lemma.
The Gumbel normalizations use quantiles b_(2m), b_n, b_(2ℓ); finite indices near 2 are excluded in limiting statements.

originality.rationale: Known symmetric-edge-polytope facet/volume structure supplies the graphical body and common tree incidence determinant, while Bibinger and standard Gaussian extreme-value theory supply isolated iid-maxima laws. The checked published Resultary tree graphical-zonotope variance paper studies the distinct Minkowski-sum zonotope, not this symmetric-edge convex hull; its width is a SUM of |coordinate differences|, whereas here the width is the MAX. The correlated-edge Chen–Stein regime and the mixed star/path critical crossover including an atom at s>0 are nontrivial geometric consequences not stated by these stronger general inputs. Historical equivalence under Gaussian network extremes terminology remains possible.
residual_risks: An unindexed correlated Gaussian max-over-graph theorem specialized to a broom may already imply the atomic crossover.
Independent checks did not replay AGG Poisson approximation numerically at very large n; proof relied on mathematical error estimates.

value.rationale: The class is geometrically natural: all tree symmetric-edge polytopes have identical combinatorial crosspolytope structure and exactly the same intrinsic volume yet exhibit genuinely different random-width laws. The half-normal, Gumbel, and atomic continuum of crossover limits provide a motivated probabilistic phase classification and concrete counterexample to width-distribution universality; the atom is not a routine finite case count.
residual_risks: The degree growth assumption is only sufficient, so no complete arbitrary-tree classification is claimed.

final_claim: For intrinsic Haar-direction widths of Q_T=conv{±(e_i−e_j):ij in E(T)}, all trees on N vertices have equal volume 2^(N−1)√N/(N−1)!; sparse-degree sequences satisfy a sharp Gumbel limit for maximum edge Gaussian differences, while broom sequences at √2 b_(2ℓ)−b_n→s have weak law max(|Z|,s), with half-normal, Gumbel and atomic crossover regimes.
limitations: No claim that degree-growth threshold is necessary or that all unbounded-degree trees are classified.
Atomic law arises in weak n→∞ limit; finite-dimensional angular-width distribution remains continuous.
